Bending of a Piecewise Developable Surface
M. I. Shtogrina
ReceivedFebruary 2011
Abstract—We substantiateindetailthe possibilityofone-parameterbending ofadevelopable
surface possessing a stationary curvilinear edge and stationary rectilinear generators. We con-
struct particular examples of developable surfaces that possess a curvilinear edge and admit
one-parameter bendings. We also give examples of closed piecewise developable surfaces that
admit one-parameter bendings.
DOI: 10.1134/S0081543811080086
The present study is a continuation of paper [1], in which we addressed the problem of recon-
structing a developable surface with a curvilinear edge in R3 from its development on the plane R2
on which the preimages of this curvilinear edge and of all rectilinear generators adjoining this edge
are specified. It turned out that such a reconstruction is possible up to an arbitrary constant C
that arises in solving the problem. The constant C can be determined from the value of the angle
made by generators at some point of the edge of the sought surface in the space R3.
Investigations of the structure of an arbitrary developable surface with a curvilinear edge were
initiated in [2]. Paper [2], in turn, is a continuation of [3] and subsequent generalizations [4–6, 17].
In [2], we began to study piecewise smooth surfaces in the particular case when the surface is
developable. It was assumed that each smooth piece of the surface is at least C2 smooth and each
curvilinearedgeisatleastC3 smooth(recallthatthetransversality oftwo smoothpiecesguarantees
only the smoothness of their intersection); hence, at each of its points, this edge has a well defined
torsion κ; all these conditions are assumed to hold throughout the present paper as well.

the geodesic r = r(s) cannot be an edge of a piecewise smooth developable surface. This means
that the preimage of a curvilinear edge of a developable surface is curvilinear on the development.
This conclusion is valid both for a space curve and for a plane curve. If a geodesic line is a
plane curve, then the rectifying developable surface is a cylinder. (The generators of the rectifying
surface coincide with the instantaneous axes of rotation of the Frenet trihedron t,n,b at the points
of the curve r = r(s). When the curve is planar, the Darboux vector κt + kb directed along
an instantaneous axis of rotation has a constant direction: it is directed along the binormal b
perpendicular to the plane of the curve, because κ = 0. Hence, in the class of smooth developable
surfaces, a geodesic line is encountered as a plane curve only when it is an orthogonal trajectory of
the family of rectilinear generators of a cylinder.) So, on a piecewise smooth developable surface, a
geodesic7 line can serve as an edge only when it is a rectilinear generator. Only a rectilinear edge
has a planar half-neighborhood [3, Ch. 8, §1]. Hence, on a piecewise smooth developable surface
consisting of a finite number of smooth pieces, any nonextendible planar piece whose boundary has
no common parts with the boundary of the surface is a polygon. An angle of the polygon may
be greater than π only at a vertex situated on the boundary of the surface. If all vertices of the
polygon are interior points of the surface, then the polygon is convex.
